name: core.openwop.workflows.data-ops
description: Real-work workflow pack (RFC 0013, ADR 0200/0201) — the Data Ops cluster, the one shape-family the Zapier/n8n and Microsoft canons don't cover (surfaced by the Make/Workato research): collapsing many records into one output (the aggregator canon), one-way movement of records between systems, and content routing (send a record down the right branch). Roll Up, Records → Table, Records → System (one-way upsert behind a human sign-off), and Content Router (route a record to the matching branch by a field predicate — the Make router shape, gated via edge conditions, ADR 0201). Uses only shipped, executable nodes (core.flow.aggregate-{numeric,text,table} + core.flow.router + core.ai.chatCompletion + core.chat.approvalGate + core.openwop.http.openapi-call + core.openwop.integration.notification-push). The write is ONE-WAY movement keyed on an external id (re-runs update, never duplicate) behind a human approval — it is NOT a bidirectional sync. All tenant values are run parameters (replay-deterministic).
author: openwop

chains.label: Roll Up a List of Records
chains.description: Turn a list of records (orders, line items, expenses…) into one narrated summary: sum a numeric field, format each record into a readable line, and write a short digest. The 'collapse many rows into one output' shape — paste a JSON array or pipe one from another workflow.

items.description: The records to roll up (a JSON array of objects).

amountField.description: The numeric field to sum across records.

lineTemplate.description: How to format each record into a line ({{field}} references).

provider.description: AI provider id for this chain's model-calling nodes. Set it to fix a provider into those nodes when the workflow is created. Leave it unset and each run uses the run's chosen provider, else the workspace's AI setting, else the host's catalog default (ADR 0903); whichever is chosen is recorded on the run, so a replay or fork uses the same one. The workspace needs a key for the provider that runs.

model.description: Model id for this chain's model-calling nodes. Must be offered by the provider in the host catalog. Leave it unset to use the provider's model from the same choice (ADR 0903).

config.systemPrompt: You are a reporting assistant. You are given a summed total and a formatted list of records. Write a short digest (under 120 words): lead with the total, then the notable items, then one observation. Do not invent numbers beyond what you are given.

inputs.title: Roll Up a List of Records

chains.label: Records → Table + Anomaly Scan
chains.description: Reshape a list of records into a clean name/value table, then have AI scan it for outliers, gaps, and things worth a second look — delivered as a notification. Paste a JSON array of records. The column set is fixed (name, value) — a chain-level `{{params.*}}` config token only substitutes STRINGS (the host's per-run config interpolation is a string-replace over the token; an array/object param collapses to its `String(...)` form, e.g. '[object Object]'), so an array-typed `columns` parameter cannot be threaded through this node's `config.columns` — it needs the real array, not a stringified one.

items.description: The records to tabulate (a JSON array of objects).

provider.description: AI provider id for this chain's model-calling nodes. Set it to fix a provider into those nodes when the workflow is created. Leave it unset and each run uses the run's chosen provider, else the workspace's AI setting, else the host's catalog default (ADR 0903); whichever is chosen is recorded on the run, so a replay or fork uses the same one. The workspace needs a key for the provider that runs.

model.description: Model id for this chain's model-calling nodes. Must be offered by the provider in the host catalog. Leave it unset to use the provider's model from the same choice (ADR 0903).

config.systemPrompt: You are a data analyst. Given a table of rows and columns, call out outliers, missing/empty values, and rows worth a second look. Be specific (cite the row). If the table looks clean, say so.

findings.description: The table plus the anomaly scan.

chains.label: Records → System (one-way)
chains.description: One-way movement: read records from a source system, reshape them with AI, review, and upsert them into a destination — keyed on an external id so re-runs update the same records instead of duplicating them. It is one-way, not a sync: it does not read the destination back, propagate deletes, or reconcile conflicts. The write step needs a connection with write scope (if you added that scope after connecting, re-authorize the connection) and an upsert-by-external-key operation (e.g. Salesforce upsert, HubSpot upsert) — pointed at a plain create it will duplicate. Every write waits on your approval.

sourceConnectionRef.description: The source connection to read from (e.g. core.openwop.connections.salesforce).

readOperationId.description: The read/list operation on the source (e.g. listContacts).

destConnectionRef.description: The destination connection to write to (e.g. core.openwop.connections.hubspot).

upsertOperationId.description: An upsert-by-external-key operation on the destination (not a plain create, which would duplicate on re-run).

keyField.description: The external-id field the upsert keys on (so re-runs update, not duplicate).

provider.description: AI provider id for this chain's model-calling nodes. Set it to fix a provider into those nodes when the workflow is created. Leave it unset and each run uses the run's chosen provider, else the workspace's AI setting, else the host's catalog default (ADR 0903); whichever is chosen is recorded on the run, so a replay or fork uses the same one. The workspace needs a key for the provider that runs.

model.description: Model id for this chain's model-calling nodes. Must be offered by the provider in the host catalog. Leave it unset to use the provider's model from the same choice (ADR 0903).

config.systemPrompt: You map source records to the destination's shape. Return a JSON array; for every field you cannot determine from the source, output the string "unknown" — never guess or invent a value that would be written to a system of record. Preserve the external key ({{params.keyField}}) on every record.

config.title: Review the reshaped records before upserting into the destination

result.description: The approved, upserted records (one-way, keyed on the external id).

chains.label: Content Router
chains.description: Route a record to the right branch by one of its fields: match on the field's value (e.g. priority high / normal / low) and only the matching branch fires its notification. Set the field to switch on; the three example branches match high, normal, and low.

value.description: The record to route (a JSON object).

routeField.description: The field on the record to route by.

routed.description: The branch the record was routed to.
